title: Environmental dependence in the halo model informed by the FLAMINGO simulations
comment: 16 pages. Prepared for submission to A&A
summary: Galaxy-galaxy lensing (GGL) measurements around galaxy samples in different environments provide valuable information about the galaxy-halo connection. In such studies the halo model is commonly used to estimate physical parameters from the lensing signal, but the impact of environment is generally not considered. Our aim is to adapt the halo model to allow a density-split GGL analysis and to understand the environmental dependence of the elements of the model. We use the FLAMINGO suite of cosmological hydrodynamical simulations to construct samples of halos in underdense and overdense regions. Environment density is assigned to halos based on halo counts within an aperture, employing different aperture sizes to probe both local and large scales. We utilize spherical apertures with radii between $1 h^{-1} {\rm Mpc}$ and $10 h^{-1} {\rm Mpc}$. We find a strong dependence on environment for the halo mass function (HMF) and the halo bias. To account for this, we propose an empirical modification that can be applied to existing HMF prescriptions. We find that after a density split, the halo bias is approximately constant with mass. There is also an environmental dependence for the stellar-to-halo-mass relation (SHMR), the conditional stellar mass function, and the mass-concentration relation, all of which can be addressed with existing models. We evaluate the impact of overlooking environment on halo occupation distribution (HOD) parameter inference, finding that it leads to biased estimations of the SHMR and the satellite fraction. These results emphasize the need to review the assumptions adopted in the halo model when working with samples of galaxies binned by environment, and consequently, by galaxy properties that correlate with environment, such as morphology and color.

title: Consistently Reproducing Early Galaxy Observations and 21-cm Signal during the Epoch of Reionization
summary: In the standard cosmological model, galaxies forming within dark matter haloes are the primary drivers of the Epoch of Reionization (EoR). The complex physics of galaxy formation introduces scatter in the relation between halo mass and star-formation activity, with implications for the production and escape of ionising photons. In this work, we implement a stochastic source model in our cosmological radiative transfer simulations. We calibrate our model against the high-redshift ultraviolet luminosity function observed by JWST and observational constraints on Lyman-continuum leakage to constrain the ionising escape fraction. We find that stochastic star formation redistributes ionising emissivity toward lower-mass haloes, producing a more fragmented ionisation topology and delaying the growth of the largest ionised regions relative to the deterministic, observationally calibrated model. However, when the two models match total ionising photon production, their global neutral fractions and 21-cm power spectrum remain nearly indistinguishable, despite small differences in the morphology of individual ionised regions. Additionally, we establish a unified framework that lets us apply source models derived from computationally expensive hydrodynamical simulations (SPICE, FIRE-2 and Thesan) and investigate their impact on large-volume reionisation simulations, extending their prescriptions to scales of >100 Mpc. We find that these prescriptions produce distinct ionisation topologies and 21-cm statistical signatures, even when their global reionisation histories are similar. Our results highlight the importance of combining physically motivated galaxy formation prescriptions from hydrodynamical simulations with large-volume radiative transfer simulations to interpret forthcoming 21-cm observations and constrain the sources of cosmic reionisation.

title: Extending SOMPZ beyond Spectroscopic Coverage for Roman Weak Lensing
summary: Precision weak lensing cosmology requires accurate galaxy redshift distributions. However, the spectroscopic samples used to characterize these distributions do not fully span the magnitude--color--redshift space of weak lensing source galaxies, necessitating extrapolation. This challenge will be critical at the depth of the Roman Space Telescope's High Latitude Imaging Survey (Roman HLIS). Using simulated LSST Year 4 and Roman HLIS photometry from the Cardinal simulations, we quantify how spectroscopic incompleteness biases photometric-redshift (photo-z) calibration and cosmological constraints. We find that the standard Self-Organizing Map p(z) (SOMPZ) method produces substantial tomographic bin overlaps and biased source redshift distributions. To address these limitations, we develop Roman-SOMPZ, which uses dedicated individual-galaxy photo-z estimators to supply redshift references for tomographic binning and redshift estimation. For the latter, we introduce UMAP-flow-z, an estimator that uses a UMAP embedding of deep-field galaxy colors to infer redshifts for phenotypes lacking spectroscopic representation. Compared with the standard pipeline, Roman-SOMPZ produces better-separated tomographic bins and lower absolute mean-redshift biases in eight of nine bins. Propagating the estimated redshift distributions into cosmological inference, we find that existing spectroscopy is adequate for early-stage weak lensing analyses in the Roman deep fields. Conversely, full medium-tier cosmology will require further improvements in redshift characterization.

title: Multimessenger Probes of Primordial Black Holes with Gravitational Wave and 21 cm Observations
summary: Primordial black holes (PBHs) formed from the collapse of curvature perturbations in the early universe are known to have an associated gravitational wave signal sourced by the same scalar perturbations. In this work, we show that there is a complementarity between these gravitational waves and modifications of the 21 cm global signal during the cosmic dark ages due to PBH evaporation. For PBHs in the range $ M_{\rm PBH} \sim 5 \times 10^{13} \, {\rm g} - 10^{17} \, {\rm g}$, there is a correlated signal in gravitational waves in the LISA, deci-Hz, and ground based regimes from $f_{\rm GW} \sim 10^{-3} \, {\rm Hz} - 20 \, {\rm Hz}$ and in the 21 cm global signal from $z \sim 300 - 30$. These observations are entirely independent of each other and within the reach of near-future experiments, making a combined measurement a novel multimessenger probe of primordial physics.

title: The evolution of 3C 306 in the galaxy cluster RXCJ1454.4+1622: linking spectral ageing, ICM conditions, and jet dynamics through MHD simulations
comment: 22 pages. Published in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
summary: We present a methodology for analysing radio sources in galaxy clusters by combining multi-frequency radio observations, X-ray analysis of the intracluster medium (ICM), and three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations, and apply it to the galaxy cluster RXCJ1454.4+1622 and its associated FR II radio galaxy 3C 306 (IC 4516). The radio emission exhibits a curved structure connecting the lobes, likely indicating a complex dynamical evolution influenced by environmental effects. Spectral index and break-frequency maps reveal a relatively homogeneous radiative ageing distribution, with characteristic spectral ages of $\sim220$ Myr and a smooth spatial gradient. From equipartition arguments, we estimate an equivalent jet magnetic field of $2.1 \pm 0.3\,μ$G, consistent with values observed in FR II radio galaxies. These observational constraints are used to initialise non-relativistic MHD simulations exploring three scenarios: jet precession, bulk motion of the source through the ICM, and a combined model including both effects. Neither pure precession nor pure source motion alone fully reproduces the observed morphology, whereas the combined model provides a more consistent representation of the jet curvature and lobe asymmetries. Nevertheless, the simulations indicate that source motion is the dominant mechanism shaping the large-scale radio morphology, with jet precession playing a secondary role. The inferred source velocity ($\sim280$ km s$^{-1}$) and precession timescale ($\sim250$ Myr) are compatible with the spectral ageing constraints. These results suggest that the morphology of 3C 306 is influenced by the interplay between jet precession and dynamical interaction with the ICM, highlighting the role of environmental effects in radio-galaxy evolution in clusters.

title: A DECADE of Giants: A catalog of 42,000 optically identified galaxy clusters from 13,000 $\mathrm{deg}^2$ of the sky
summary: Galaxy clusters are sensitive to a rich variety of physics spanning a wide dynamic range, from microphysical to cosmological scales. Optical datasets are efficient at identifying clusters and studying their properties. We leverage 13,000 $\rm deg^2$ of the sky imaged by the Dark Energy Camera (DECam) and extract over 40,000 clusters using the redMaPPer algorithm. Our catalog spans $0.2 < z < 0.9$ and $M_{\rm 200c} \gtrsim 10^{14} {\rm M}_{\odot}/h$, with four-band ($griz$) photometric redshifts that have a precision $σ_z/(1 + z) \leq 0.008$ below $z < 0.65$, and $\leq 0.011$ between $0.65 < z < 0.9$ and that exhibit an outlier rate of $f_{\rm out} < 0.2\%$. Our cluster finding is calibrated using spectroscopic data, but we find that a larger spectroscopic sample does not improve the performance of our cluster redshift estimation. We cross-match our catalog to those produced from millimeter-wave and X-ray data, and extract scaling relations between various cluster observables. There is excellent agreement between our estimates for different subsets of the 13,000 ${\rm deg}^2$ dataset, and also with results from prior catalogs and simulations. We use our joint analysis of millimeter-wave and optical data to estimate the halo masses of individual clusters. We also provide lensing profiles, measured for each cluster using overlapping galaxy shape catalogs, to enable additional mass-calibration work from the community. We demonstrate from a suite of tests that spatial inhomogeneity in the quality of the imaging data does not have an appreciable impact on the properties of this catalog. We also test a cylindrical richness observable, which is defined such that it is significantly simpler to model, and show that it has precision competitive with the traditional optical richness observable. All data products and measurements are made publicly available.

title: Modeling Multi-band Active Galactic Nuclei Lightcurves Using an Self-supervised Attentive Neural Process Network
summary: With the the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST), observations of tens of millions of quasars are expected. We present a machine-learning framework based on an attentive neural process (ANP) that models stochastic quasar variability and jointly performs two tasks: (i) probabilistic reconstruction of quasar light curves in all six LSST bands, and (ii) inference of physical parameters of the AGN system --- black hole mass, Eddington ratio, and intrinsic variability timescale --- with joint, full-covariance posteriors. The model processes all six bands within a single masked attention mechanism, so that observations in any band constrain the shared driving process, and natively handles irregularly and asynchronously sampled light curves with realistic heteroscedastic noise. We train and evaluate on full ten-year light curves simulated with a relativistic accretion-disk reprocessing model, observed through the fielded Rubin baseline cadence with per-visit photometric noise. The light-curve model is trained with self-supervised, learning from the sparse noisy observations alone and never accessing the underlying noiseless light curves. On a held-out test set, we show that our ANP model reach comparable performances to that of the near-optimal baseline Gaussian process model, while exceeding it in power spectrum reconstruction and damped-random walk timescale estimation. The compact learned latent representation supports future downstream applications, and the fully observation-driven training objective enables direct fine-tuning on real LSST light curves.

title: Critical magnetic Reynolds number of the weakly-collisional turbulent dynamo in supersonic plasmas
summary: Weakly-collisional plasmas are found in several turbulent astrophysical environments, such as the Intra-galaxy-cluster medium (ICM) and the solar wind, where magnetic fields can be amplified by the turbulent dynamo. The onset of dynamo action is determined by the critical magnetic Reynolds number, ${\rm Rm}_{\rm crit}$, above which turbulent motions amplify magnetic energy. Although ${\rm Rm}_{\rm crit}$ has been studied extensively in collisional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) turbulence, its value in supersonic weakly-collisional plasmas remains unknown. Here we determine ${\rm Rm}_{\rm crit}$ using three-dimensional hybrid particle-in-cell (HPIC) simulations of solenoidally driven turbulence with a sonic Mach number $\approx 2$. We vary the magnetic Reynolds number over ${\rm Rm}\approx31$-$1000$ and consider two initial plasma magnetisations, characterised by initial Larmor ratios $r_{\rm Larmor, 0}/L_{\rm box}=1$ and $100$. We find that the magnetic energy grows exponentially at sufficiently large ${\rm Rm}$ and decays when magnetic diffusion dominates at low ${\rm Rm}$. By fitting the magnetic-energy growth rate as a function of ${\rm Rm}$, we measure ${\rm Rm}_{\rm crit}=190^{+21}_{-17}$ and $198^{+16}_{-18}$ for the initially magnetised and unmagnetised plasma, respectively. These values are the same within their uncertainties, indicating that the initial plasma magnetisation does not significantly affect ${\rm Rm}_{\rm crit}$ in the supersonic regime. The measured values are higher than those previously obtained for the subsonic weakly-collisional dynamo, showing that increasing compressibility makes weakly-collisional turbulent dynamo action more difficult to excite. The measured values are also approximately 1.5 times higher than the ${\rm Rm}_{\rm crit}$ value reported for supersonic MHD turbulence.

title: Models of spectral bumps of primary cosmic rays and multi-messenger tests
summary: The energy spectra of individual species of cosmic ray nuclei by recent direct detection experiments show complicated structures with spectral hardenings and softenings rather than featureless power laws, which challenge the traditional understanding of the production, acceleration, and propagation of cosmic rays. Particularly, the DAMPE measurements reveal charge-dependent softenings and reject mass-dependent softenings with a high significance. Taking into account the correlated structures at similar energies in the large-scale anisotropies of cosmic rays, one of the most natural interpretations of the spectral structures is the presence of a nearby cosmic ray source. In this case, the softening energies correspond to the acceleration upper limits of such a source, forming the so-called Peters cycle of the spectra. Alternative models such as the injection/acceleration and propagation models may also reproduce the spectral bumps, but show difficulty to explain the anisotropies. Fluxes of secondary nuclei and $γ$ rays offer additional tests of different models. Future multi-messenger observations are expected to be able to pin down the origin of cosmic rays.

title: Galactic warps constrain equivalence-principle violation in the dark sector
comment: 11+3 pages, 3 figures; to be submitted to Phys. Rev. D
summary: Current measurements of the expansion of the Universe allow for the presence of evolving dark energy, distinct from a cosmological constant, with an equation of state that seems to violate the null energy condition. One notable explanation for this behaviour is that the dark energy interacts with the dark matter, violating the equivalence principle yet evading conventional laboratory and astrophysical constraints. Such models produce fifth forces acting only on dark matter. We show how such forces separate halo and stellar disk centres, creating a potential gradient across the disk that warps it into a cup shape. Measuring the warps of $4\times10^3$ edge-on disks in Sloan Digital Sky Survey images and modelling the fifth-force signal together with competing baryonic effects, we find no sign of the predicted correlation between the measured warps and the fifth-force field. This constrains the fifth-force strength relative to gravity to $ΔG/G_N<7.7\times10^{-4}$ at 95% credibility (or $<1.7\times10^{-3}$ once systematic uncertainties are included) for force ranges of 8 Mpc and above. In the infinite-range limit of a scalar rolling today, even the conservative bound is three times stronger than the tightest cosmological bound (which, unlike ours, depends on the scalar's cosmological evolution) and about two orders of magnitude below other astrophysical bounds. It disfavours at 2-3$σ$ the couplings preferred by recent fits of interacting dark energy to cosmological data unless gravitational screening is invoked.

title: Clumpy Outflows from Super-Eddington Accreting Black Holes. II. Conditions for Clump Formation
summary: Active galactic nuclei (AGNs) commonly exhibit ultra-fast outflows (UFOs) with velocities of $0.03$--$0.3~c$. Recent high-resolution X-ray observations with XRISM/Resolve suggest that UFOs may have a clumpy structure. However, the formation and evolution of these clumpy outflows remain poorly understood. In the first paper of this series, we investigated the formation of clumpy outflows using numerical simulations and find that sufficiently high spatial resolution is required to reproduce clumpy structures numerically. In this second paper, we perform a series of numerical experiments to identify the key physical processes governing clump formation. We find that spatial fluctuations of physical quantities at the disk surface are essential for the formation of clumpy outflows, whereas spatial and temporal fluctuations at the inner boundary have only a minor effect. Furthermore, density structure-function analysis suggests that the high-density regions have an elongated morphology with characteristic transverse widths of several tens of $R_{\rm g}$, possibly produced by radiation Rayleigh--Taylor instability. A more comprehensive investigation of the instability in general-relativistic radiation magnetohydrodynamic simulations, where accretion disk structures emerge self-consistently, is expected to provide deeper insights into the physical origin of clumpy outflows.

title: Impact of Residual Gain Errors on the Detectability of Ionized Bubbles during Reionization with SKA 21-cm observations
summary: Detecting ionized bubbles and characterizing their properties and the surrounding intergalactic medium (IGM) using the HI 21-cm signal provides direct probes of cosmic reionization. Here, we focus on the detection of individual ionized bubbles around luminous sources using a matched-filter technique. We investigate the impact of time- and frequency-correlated residual antenna gain errors on the detectability and characterization of individual ionized regions with SKA-Low. We simulate mock SKA-Low AA* observations that include the HI 21-cm signal, astrophysical foregrounds, residual gain errors, and system noise corresponding to 100 h of observing time. We subtract the foreground components from the gain-corrupted data and subsequently apply the matched-filter technique to the residual visibilities. We find that the matched-filter technique is able to detect the ionized bubble and constrain its properties in the presence of residual gain errors with the rms amplitudes up to $σ_A\sim1\%$ and rms phases up to $σ_φ\sim1^\circ$. Residual gain errors at similar levels prevent the reliable identification of ionized regions in reconstructed HI 21-cm images and bias the estimated HI 21-cm power spectrum. Furthermore, we find that increasing the temporal correlation length increases the level of gain-induced artifacts in the reconstructed image. In contrast, increasing the frequency correlation length reduces these artifacts, as some fraction of the spectrally smooth gain-induced residuals is removed during foreground subtraction. We further find that the inferred bubble and IGM parameters remain largely unaffected by residual gain errors, although their uncertainties can increase. These results demonstrate the potential and robustness of the matched-filter technique for detecting and characterizing individual ionized bubbles in the presence of substantial residual calibration errors.

title: Tidal Disruption Events in Active Galactic Nuclei: Thermal Radiation and Jets
summary: Over the past decade, dozens of Tidal Disruption Events (TDEs) have been identified, with many more expected from upcoming surveys. A small subset has been observed to launch transient, highly luminous relativistic jets, for which the origin of the requisite magnetic flux has not been identified. A non-negligible fraction of TDEs are expected in Active Galactic Nuclei (AGNs), where a magnetized accretion flow is already present. As shown first by Chan et al. (2019), the collision of a TDE debris stream with this flow can substantially alter both disk and debris dynamics, leading to a possibly Eddington-limited flare. Here, we use the Athena++ radiation magnetohydrodynamic (RMHD) code to simulate the time near peak fallback rate of a TDE in an AGN, studying the debris-disk interaction, the radiation emitted, and the accumulation of magnetic flux near the horizon. In the example simulated, the accretion rate climbs to $\sim 12\,\dot{M}_{ \rm Edd}$, while the escaping solid angle-integrated luminosity approaches $\sim L_{ \rm Edd}$. The photon luminosity is strongly asymmetric, brighter in the hemisphere from which the debris strikes the disk and dimmer in the hemisphere toward which the debris travels. The photon spectrum peaks in the EUV. The polar magnetic flux grows $\sim 33$-fold, enough to raise the Blandford--Znajek luminosity by a factor $\sim 10^3$, reaching a level sufficient to power observed TDE jets. The polar magnetic flux is also asymmetric, likely making any jet similarly asymmetric, but in the opposite sense to the photon flux.

title: Beyond dust in local cosmography: perturbative Vlasov predictions
summary: The dust approximation used in cosmography neglects the velocity dispersion generated during structure formation. This dispersion produces isotropic and anisotropic pressure, whose gradients accelerate the mean matter flow even though individual particles follow geodesics. The acceleration introduces an intrinsic dipole into the local distance-redshift relation. We calculate this dipole and the accompanying changes in expansion and shear using linear Vlasov perturbation theory about an FLRW background, with a mean dispersion history motivated by halo estimates. The assumed FLRW background prevents an independent test of the cosmological principle; the numerical predictions also depend on the adopted LCDM cosmology. Pressure also changes the growth of structure, modifying the shear and the spatial gradients that govern how the distance anisotropy varies with redshift. The largest correction at the lowest order in redshift is to the shear, while changes in the expansion gradient can produce a larger dipole at the next order. The resulting intrinsic dipole is far smaller than the observed low-redshift dipole, whose behaviour nearest the observer is dominated by motion between the matter and CMB frames.

title: Statistical Analysis of Neutron Star Cooling: Implications for the Nuclear Equation of State and Nucleon Pairing
summary: We perform a statistical analysis of the thermal evolution of isolated neutron stars by confronting theoretical cooling curves with luminosity-age measurements for 24 sources. For each object, we explore five purely nucleonic equations of state (APR4, FSU2R, DD2, IST, and NL3$ωρ$) combined with representative models of neutron superfluidity and proton superconductivity, while varying the gravitational mass and envelope composition. The analysis spans approximately $10^5$ cooling curves. Within this framework, we find that only the NL3$ωρ$ equation of state and, to a lesser extent, IST, both including neutron triplet pairing, provide an overall satisfactory description of the data. The remaining equations of state are in significant tension with the observations. These results demonstrate that NS cooling provides complementary constraints on dense matter, alongside nuclear structure, global NS observables, and gravitational-wave observations, while probing the interplay between the EoS and nucleon pairing.

title: A Morphology-Based Cross-Tracer Ratio for Robust BAO Tests
summary: We use the Cross-Tracer Clustering Ratio (CTCR) acoustic response estimator, a new probe of morphology-dependent galaxy clustering in photometric surveys. CTCR is the ratio of the auto-power spectrum of early-type galaxies (ETGs) to their cross-power spectrum with late-type galaxies (LTGs). In the matched-kernel deterministic linear-bias limit the CTCR cancels the complete projected matter spectrum, including the baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) wiggles, leaving only the relative linear bias. This makes the ratio uniquely sensitive to physics beyond deterministic linear bias: any residual acoustic structure in the CTCR must arise from a difference between the normalised non-linear responses of the two tracers. We, for the first time, exploit this property to model the measured ratio as a smooth scale-dependent baseline multiplied by a scale-dependent acoustic template, and constrain the amplitude $A_{\rm morph}$ of the differential acoustic response jointly with the BAO dilation parameter $α$. Applying the estimator to nine bins of the DESI Legacy Survey Data Release 8 spanning $0.1 < z < 0.9$, we obtain$α= 0.9997 \pm 0.0383$, consistent with the Planck 2018 $Λ$CDM prediction, and $A_{\rm morph} = 0.369 \pm 0.307$, consistent with zero. A Bayesian model comparison yields at most a 2.6$σ$ preference for the acoustic template over a smooth-only baseline. The estimator is model-independent, requires no external calibration of the absolute bias, and is directly applicable to the wide-field imaging surveys that will define the next decade of cosmology. It offers a new route to testing halo occupation and assembly-bias models, and an independent, systematics-robust cross-check of BAO measurements from spectroscopic surveys.

title: Hyperonic Direct-Urca Neutrino Emission with Lattice-QCD-Informed Form Factors
summary: We investigate the sensitivity of direct-Urca neutrino emission in hyperonic neutron-star matter to the structure and momentum dependence of baryonic transition form factors. Using the zero-temperature FSU2H relativistic mean-field equation of state, we derive the relativistic emissivity for general spin-$1/2$ baryon transitions with the complete six form-factor contribution. We compare conventional static flavor-SU(3) couplings with vacuum lattice-QCD-informed form factors, using direct lattice vacuum input for $n\rightarrow p$ and $Λ\rightarrow p$ and a hybrid construction for the remaining hyperonic channels. Evaluating the latter both at $q^2=0$ and at the kinetic momentum transfer sampled at the Fermi surfaces separates changes in the zero-momentum couplings from momentum-transfer effects. The sensitivity is strongly channel dependent. The nucleonic transition probes $q^2\simeq0$ and is only weakly affected, whereas hyperonic channels can sample substantially larger momentum transfers and receive correspondingly larger corrections. These modifications propagate to the integrated neutrino luminosity of stellar configurations. Our results estimate the possible scale of the sensitivity coming from momentum transfer dependence, absent from static-coupling treatments and motivate future first-principles studies of baryonic weak currents in dense matter.

title: Hostbusters: constraining $H_0$ and binary formation channels through gravitational-wave host galaxy associations
summary: Gravitational-wave dark sirens can be combined with galaxy catalogues to provide a measurement of the Hubble constant. This inference requires assigning each potential host galaxy a probability of hosting a merger, but the appropriate weighting is uncertain because the binary merger rate may trace different galaxy properties, such as stellar mass or star formation rate, depending on the underlying formation channel. We introduce a flexible framework in which the dark-siren population is described as a mixture of two host-weighting prescriptions, with the mixing fraction inferred jointly with $H_0$. These components may be interpreted as subpopulations associated with distinct binary-formation environments. Using simulated catalogues, we show that marginalising over uncertainty in the host-population mixture preserves unbiased constraints on $H_0$, while allowing the gravitational-wave data to constrain the relative contribution of the two host populations. In particular, an A#-like detector network with $\mathcal{O}(10^3)$ dark sirens may be able to exclude scenarios in which the host population traces only one of the two weighting prescriptions. Dark-siren analyses may therefore provide robust cosmological measurements and new information about how merging compact binaries trace the galaxy population.

title: Constraints on the Progenitor of SN 2023bee from its Nebular-Phase Spectra
summary: We present late-time photometry (~100-400 days after peak) and nebular-phase optical/NIR spectroscopy (100-360 days) of the Type Ia supernova (SN Ia) SN 2023bee. This SN Ia was observed TESS immediately before and after explosion and showed a relatively weak early excess light-curve feature detected in multiple UV and optical bands. Possible explanations for this early excess feature include interaction between the SN ejecta and a non-degenerate companion, or the decay of radioactive isotopes synthesized near the ejecta surface in a sub-$\text{M}_\text{Ch}$ double-detonation scenario. However, the degeneracies and incompleteness of existing models have so far prevented a definitive conclusion about its progenitor system. Nebular-phase spectra provide a complementary probe of SN Ia progenitors by constraining stripped H/He-rich material and iron-group abundances sensitive to the progenitor white dwarf density. We report the non-detection of narrow H/He features in nebular phase optical/NIR spectra of SN 2023bee, placing upper limits of $m^{\text{stripped}}_\text{H}\lesssim5.0\times10^{-3}\text{ M}_\odot$ and $m_\text{He}^{\text{stripped}}\lesssim1.2\times10^{-4}\text{ M}_\odot$. These limits strongly disfavor a non-degenerate companion and suggest that companion interaction is unlikely to explain the early excess of SN 2023bee. We also performed line-diagnostic measurements on the 7200 Åcomplex using multi-Gaussian fitting and continuum estimation, with the inferred velocities validated against NIR spectrum at the similar phase. The resulting low Ni-to-Fe mass ratio, $m_\text{Ni}/m_\text{Fe}\lesssim 0.06$, is broadly consistent with a sub-$M_{\text{Ch}}$ double-detonation progenitor system.

title: Constraints on the Cosmic Expansion Rate Using the DECam Local Volume Exploration Survey and the Fifth Gravitational Wave Transient Catalog
comment: 9 Pages, 6 Figures, 2 Tables, Submitted to A&A
summary: Gravitational-wave standard sirens provide a calibration-free measure of distances, offering important input on the long-standing tension between early- and late-Universe measurements of the Hubble constant ($H_0$). In the absence of an electromagnetic counterpart, the dark siren method can be employed to statistically correlate a gravitational wave event's localization with a galaxy catalog of potential hosts. We present a measurement of the Hubble constant using the DECam Local Volume Exploration Survey Data Release 3 and the fifth Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog. Applying the dark siren method to a large, photometrically heterogeneous footprint required revised catalog-construction choices: a faint apparent-magnitude threshold ($m_r<20$) to control known photometric-redshift bias, a bright apparent-magnitude threshold ($m_r>15.5$) to exclude saturated sources, implementation of an evolving luminosity function parameterization, and de-biasing survey regions based on survey depth and photometric redshift precision. With these choices applied to DELVE, we obtain $H_0= 67.4^{+13.0}_{-11.2}\ \mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ from dark sirens alone, and $H_0= 70.6^{+8.7}_{-7.0}\ \mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ when combined with the bright siren GW170817. We test other galaxy catalog configuration choices, and find subdominant influence from photometric band choice and luminosity function parameterization on the final $H_0$ posterior. Our results demonstrate that extending the dark siren method to wider-area, non-uniform galaxy surveys is feasible and provides additional constraining power on $H_0$ relative to the spectral siren method, opening the door for analyses with forthcoming galaxy catalogs from LSST, Euclid, and Roman.

title: Pulse Morphology and Spectral Study of LPT J1634+44 Using GMRT
comment: 18 pages, 9 figures, 3 tables, submitted to ApJ, comments are welcome
summary: Long-period radio transients (LPTs) are a recently discovered class of Galactic coherent radio emitters characterized by rotation periods of minutes to hours and highly polarized radio pulses. Their nature remains uncertain, with proposed scenarios invoking isolated or binary systems containing neutron stars (NSs) or white dwarfs (WDs). We investigate the nature of CHIME/ILT J1634+44 through multi-band observations with the Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (GMRT), examining its pulse morphology, spectral evolution, and timing behavior. The pulses show substantial profile variability, and the subpulse features evolve significantly across observing frequencies. Using our measurements of quasi-periodic microstructures in J1634+44 pulses as well as those of other LPTs available from literature, we show that the scaling relationship between the rotation and microstructure periods is not limited to only neutron stars but extend to white dwarfs as well. The radio spectrum of J1634+44 is highly variable and exhibits a spectral turnover that shifts toward lower frequencies across observing epochs. Interpreting this turnover as free-free absorption, we constrain the physical properties of the intervening absorbing medium. Complementing these emission diagnostics, we also present analysis of pulse arrival times spanning approximately a decade to probe the previously proposed spin-orbit resonance models for this LPT.

title: Gravitational Instability of Cold Axion Dark Matter Beyond Minimal Coupling
summary: Following recent observations of unexpectedly massive galaxies at high redshift by the James Webb Space Telescope, the revision of Dark Matter (DM) models --specifically regarding how DM couples to gravity-- has become a central topic in Cosmology. In this paper, we develop an axion model for Cold Dark Matter (CDM) with a non-minimal coupling to gravity. From this framework, we evaluate the gravitational instability in the hydrodynamic limit. Our results demonstrate how gravitational instabilities depend on the non-minimal coupling parameter, providing a novel tool for aligning with the high-redshift observations from the James Webb Space Telescope.

title: Probing the Interstellar Medium towards the Double Pulsar and the Gum Nebula using Low-Frequency Pulse Broadening Measurements
comment: 22 pages, 6 figures, 10 tables, accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: Long-term timing of the double pulsar system (PSR J0737-3039A/B) has enabled some of the most stringent constraints on strong-field gravity. Yet, despite the system's high profile, there have been very few observations at frequencies below 300 MHz, where pulse broadening due to interstellar scattering becomes significant. Measurements of the pulse broadening timescale and its frequency scaling, $τ_\mathrm{s}\proptoν^α$ (where $α$ is the scattering spectral index), provide valuable constraints on the structure of the scattering medium. Here we report on simultaneous observations of J0737-3039A and five other nearby pulsars (J0630-3824, J0742-2822, J0820-4114, J0835-4510, J0837-4135) in the frequency range 109-231 MHz using the Murchison Widefield Array (MWA). These observations have enabled the highest-quality detections ever published for these pulsars at low frequencies. For J0737-3039A, J0742-2822, and J0837-4135, we measure $α$ to be -4.1(1), -3.8(1), and -4.1(1), respectively. These measurements provide new constraints on the density and turbulence parameters of the Gum Nebula region, and we discuss implications for models of the Galactic electron density distribution. Our current data yield a dispersion measure (DM) precision of ~4 x 10^-4 pc/cm^-3 for J0737-3039A, which can be further improved with the MWA Phase III to reach ~1 x 10^-4 pc/cm^-3, far exceeding the precision of previous studies. The prospects for precisely constraining temporal variations in the DM and pulse broadening timescale strengthen the importance of regular monitoring of J0737-3039A at low frequencies, with the eventual goal of contributing to long-term timing studies.

title: Late-time distance consistency and model-independent curvature inference with strong lensing, quasars, and galaxy clusters
comment: 18 pages, 6 figures, Accepted for publication in Research in Astronomy and Astrophysics (RAA)
summary: We revisit a late-time, model-independent distance-consistency framework that combines strong gravitational lensing systems (SGLS), ultraviolet/X-ray quasars (QSOs), and 38 Sunyaev--Zel'dovich/X-ray galaxy-cluster angular-diameter distances. The analysis focuses on systematics rather than on presenting a competitive curvature measurement. Starting from the 158-system SGLS catalog, we exclude 30 systems that violate the lensing-geometric requirement $D_{A,ls}/D_{A,s}<1$ in the isothermal reference case $γ_{\rm lens}=2$, leaving a fixed 128-system SGLS parent sample for cross-matching with 1598 QSOs. A deterministic maximum-cardinality, minimum-mismatch one-to-one assignment yields 100 SGLS--QSO pairs at the nominal $Δd/d=5\%$ threshold. We propagate the measured X-ray flux uncertainties and the intrinsic QSO scatter, and, crucially, we include the full $38\times38$ covariance induced by using the same QSO distances in the kernel-smoothed cluster predictions. With $Ω_K\sim\mathcal{U}[-10,10]$, the joint posterior is $Ω_K=2.085^{+1.634}_{-1.103}$ (68\%; central 95\% interval $[0.269,6.028]$). We do not interpret the positive shift as evidence for an open Universe. \added{This positive posterior offset is driven by cross-probe calibration tensions, sample-assignment effects, and the cluster anchor; it cannot be attributed to the intrinsic spatial geometry of the Universe.} The SGLS+QSO data alone leave curvature essentially prior dominated, $Ω_K=0.70^{+6.33}_{-7.12}$, whereas removing only the off-diagonal cluster covariance moves the posterior to $Ω_K=5.21^{+2.46}_{-2.07}$. Thus the cluster anchor supplies most of the curvature constraining power and its covariance materially changes the posterior location.

title: The accretion flow and jet of M87: broadband modelling across spatial scales
summary: The nearby radio galaxy M87 is an ideal laboratory for studying accretion flows and relativistic jet emission. The EHT collaboration conducted the most comprehensive multi-wavelength observational campaign of M87, in which radio instruments with resolutions ranging from tens of microarcseconds to about an arcsecond sampled different portions of the outflow. We model these data using a radiatively inefficient accretion flow (RIAF) with winds and a new multi-zone jet model, initially magnetically dominated, in which we solve the transport equation for the non-thermal electrons as they are injected, advected, and cooled along the jet. We then compare each radio flux with the jet emission within an effective aperture set by the angular scale of the corresponding observation. The comparison across spatial scales favours a scenario in which the RIAF, rather than the jet, produces the compact $230~{\rm GHz}$ emission, while the jet dominates the lower-frequency radio, optical/UV and X-ray emission, but cannot produce the observed $γ$-rays. The RIAF connects the Bondi-scale gas supply to an accretion rate at the horizon of $1.1\times 10^{-5}$ of the Eddington rate, consistent with EHT polarimetry, and the two jets carry about a quarter of the accretion power, $1.2\times10^{43}~{\rm erg~s}^{-1}$ each. The framework presented in this work provides a simple way to disentangle the accretion-flow and jet contributions to the emission from nearby radio galaxies.

title: Linear gas mass density: a unifying descriptor of Cosmic Filaments
summary: Cosmic filaments connect the nodes of the large-scale web and are thought to harbour a substantial fraction of the low-z baryon budget, yet a physically motivated framework for organising their diverse gas properties has been lacking. Here we show that the linear mass density $Λ$ = M_gas/L_fil, measured within the entropy radius r_K (the peak of the radial gas entropy profile) plays this role, analogous to mass in halo physics. Using TNG300-1 at z=0, we characterise the structural, thermodynamic, and chemical properties of 5637 filaments spanning more than two decades in $Λ$. Filaments form a continuous thermodynamic sequence with $Λ$, ranging from long, thin, cool, metal-poor structures to shorter, wider, hotter, and more enriched ones, with core temperatures spanning two orders of magnitude across the full WHIM window. The ratio of mass- to volume-weighted temperature reveals a shift in heat distribution: low-$Λ$ filaments have their hotter gas preferentially associated with denser material, whereas in high-$Λ$ filaments the hotter gas is diffuse. Well-defined scaling relations connect $Λ$ to temperature, electron density, pressure, entropy, and metallicity, with the T-$Λ$ scaling qualitatively consistent with gravitational heating. We present the first measurement of the gaseous linear mass density function, revealing a broad distribution with a flat low-$Λ$ regime and a steep exponential decline at high $Λ$, analogous to the halo mass function. The integrated Compton-y parameter $Y^{\rm int}$ scales systematically with $Λ$, providing a tSZ proxy accessible to current surveys. Finally, galaxy richness per unit length correlates tightly with $Λ$ (Pearson r=0.80), enabling $Λ$-based classification of filaments from spectroscopic surveys alone and guiding targeted searches for the missing baryons in the cosmic web.

title: Detection Forecasting for Blazars at MeV Energies with Fermi-LAT Swift-BAT Cross Match
summary: Over the past two decades, the lack of an MeV $γ$-ray all-sky instrument has left an observational gap in blazar broadband emission. Recently, a new suite of MeV $γ$-ray instruments with sensitivity in the $10^{-11}$ to $10^{-12}$ $\mathrm{erg/cm^{2}/s}$ range has been proposed, with the potential to far surpass the capabilities of previous all-sky MeV instruments. In this work, we forecast the capabilities of future MeV $γ$-ray instruments including COSI, GRAMS, newASTROGAM, and AMEGO-X to observe blazars. We pair total source count estimates of blazar luminosity functions with SED-modeled flux estimates of 76 blazars selected from a sample of 115 blazars cross-matched between the latest Fermi-LAT and Swift-BAT catalogs. We forecast that an instrument with a sensitivity limit of $10^{-11}$ $\mathrm{erg/cm^{2}/s}$ could detect 61 of the 76 SED-modeled blazars, and expect a total population of a few tens to a few hundreds of Flat-Spectrum Radio Quasars (FSRQs), as well as a few hundred BL Lacs (BLLs). An instrument with a sensitivity limit of $10^{-12}$ $\mathrm{erg/cm^{2}/s}$ could detect all 76 of the SED-modeled blazars, and we expect a total population of a few hundred to one thousand FSRQs and roughly one thousand BLLs. As MeV blazars have been observed to be extremely luminous and MeV $γ$-rays are minimally attenuated by the extragalactic background light, we use luminosity functions to estimate that blazars could be detected out to $z\approx6$. Lastly, we demonstrate detectability for blazars that have been proposed as neutrino-emitting candidates, as the MeV regime could provide a window into resolving lepto-hadronic degeneracies.

title: Joint Fit of Galaxy Cluster Scaling Relations from Individual Weak Lensing Data: Comparison with Stacked Analysis and a Real Data Test
comment: 31 pages, 24 figures, to be submitted to the Open Journal of Astrophysics
summary: Stacking is the standard route to signal-to-noise in cluster weak lensing, but it destroys the cluster-by-cluster information that scaling-relation studies need. We instead fit every cluster's individual $ΔΣ$ profile simultaneously, tying its mass and concentration to its own richness, redshift and magnitude gap, and compare with two stacked analyses of the same data: a forward-modelled stack sharing the same model and priors, and the standard two-step analysis. The magnitude gap (the BCG-to-brightest-satellite magnitude difference) enters the concentration, which the fossil-group picture ties to earlier assembly and more relaxed systems. On mock populations with triaxial haloes and miscentering, at DES Y3-like and LSST-like density, all three analyses recover the injected gap slope $γ_{\mathrm{cm}}$ with uncertainties that match the scatter between realisations, but not equally precisely: the joint fit scatters 1.2--1.3 times less than the forward-modelled stack, and 2 (DES-like) to 6.5 (LSST-like) times less than the two-step analysis, which is also biased in several other scaling-relation parameters. Applied to WaZP clusters with DES Y3 shears, the joint and forward-modelled fits agree on the gap coupling once the mass at fixed richness also depends on the gap, $γ_{\mathrm{cm}} = 0.065 \pm 0.033$ (forward-modelled) and$0.007^{+0.032}_{-0.033}$~mag$^{-1}$ (joint); the joint value is consistent with no coupling, so neither is a detection. The mass--concentration slope is consistent with zero in both, as expected from the upturn of the \citet{diemer2019} relation over this mass range. A gap coupling obtained in a model where the gap enters only the concentration need not survive a modest extension of that model.

title: Deep X-ray Observations of the Gamma-ray Bright Pulsar Wind Nebula HESS J1303-631
comment: Submitted to ApJ, 10 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables
summary: HESS J1303$-$631 is an evolved, TeV-bright pulsar wind nebula (PWN) powered by the energetic radio pulsar PSR~J1301$-$6305, offset by $\approx7'$ northwest of the TeV centroid, with an energy-dependent gamma-ray morphology. We present new, deep joint Chandra (108 ks) and XMM-Newton (102 ks) observations of this field. High-resolution Chandra ACIS imaging resolves the pulsar from a neighboring point source that XMM-Newton cannot separate. The pulsar's 2-10 keV spectrum is well described by an absorbed power law with $Γ=2.02\pm1.04$ and an unabsorbed luminosity of $3.44\times10^{31}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$ at $d=4.7$ kpc. Chandra also reveals faint diffuse emission east of the pulsar: a clumpy compact nebula on arcsecond scales ($Γ=2.98\pm0.53$, $L_X=4.15\times10^{31}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$) and a fainter extended nebula on arcminute scales ($Γ=1.20\pm1.25$, $L=4.36\times10^{31}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$). This morphology, the hard GeV counterpart, and the energy-dependent TeV emission together support an evolved, synchrotron-underluminous PWN whose X-ray nebula is far more compact than its TeV nebula. We also serendipitously discovered a transient X-ray source, CXOU~J130131.0$-$625919, in one of the nine new Chandra observations. Its hard spectrum ($Γ=1.4\pm0.3$) and 0.5-7\,keV luminosity of $3.34\times10^{32}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$ at a fiducial distance of 3 kpc, together with a plausible near-infrared counterpart, most closely match a flare from a young pre-main-sequence star, though an active binary or compact-object binary is not excluded. Its large offset from HESS J1303$-$631 makes association with the TeV source unlikely.

title: Exploring the Evidence for Evolving Dark Energy with the Jeffreys prior
comment: 15 pages, to be submitted to OJA, code available at https://github.com/JoshL965/Jeffreys-prior-project
summary: We investigate the impact of applying the uninformative Jeffreys prior in a re-analysis of DESI DR2 BAO, Planck 2018 CMB, and Type Ia Supernovae (DES-SN5YR, DES-Dovekie, Pantheon+, Union3). We incorporate this prior into new posterior inference and evidence calculations. We introduce novel techniques for interpreting the Jeffreys prior physically. To overcome the computational expense of the Jeffreys prior, we develop a fully $\texttt{JAX}$-based pipeline consisting of $\texttt{CosmoPower-JAX}$ emulators, gradient-based posterior inference using the No-U-Turn Sampler (NUTS), and evidence calculations using $\texttt{JAX}$-accelerated nested sampling. We demonstrate that while the parameter constraints on $w_0$ and $w_a$ remain robust to prior choice (exhibiting only minor shifts of the marginalised posterior towards the $\textit{Maximum A Posteriori}$ in less constraining dataset combinations), the Bayesian evidence is highly sensitive to the use of the Jeffreys prior; replacing uniform priors with the Jeffreys prior reverses the model-selection preference in dataset combinations that favour dynamical dark energy under the uniform prior, while strengthening existing preferences for $Λ$CDM. This is driven primarily by the significantly larger Occam penalty applied by the Jeffreys prior which penalises the overfitting of the data by a $w_0w_a$CDM model.

title: X-ray Comptonization in an Accreting Kerr Black Hole System with a Tilted Disc and Thermal Corona; A General-Relativistic Monte Carlo Simulation: I. Model, Radiative Transfer and Spectral-Timing Properties
summary: Quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in the X-ray emission of accreting black hole binaries are commonly attributed to the relativistic Lense--Thirring precession of the inner accretion flow, in which a hot inner flow, tilted with respect to the black hole spin axis, precesses as a solid body while a cooler outer disc remains at its own, different tilt -- a warped, Bardeen--Petterson-type geometry. Testing this picture requires a radiative-transfer model that self-consistently follows photons through such a system: from emission near the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO), through Compton scattering in a hot corona, to possible reflection off the misaligned outer disc, all under the full effects of light bending in Kerr spacetime. In this first paper of a two-part series, we present a general-relativistic Monte Carlo (GRMC) radiative-transfer model of a misaligned, warped, two-zone accretion system around a Kerr black hole. We describe the disc--corona geometry, the seed-photon prescription, the photon-transport engine -- including the geodesic integration scheme, the coronal Compton-scattering module and the outer-disc reflection treatment -- and the observer pipeline used to construct energy spectra, photon path-length and arrival-time distributions. We present the resulting energy spectra, light curves and spectral lags as functions of the black hole mass, corona size, outer-disc geometry, reflection albedo, photon-injection radius and observer inclination, and show how gravitational light bending systematically lengthens the path-length and arrival-time distributions of the escaping radiation. This model and its spectral-timing predictions form the foundation for Paper II, which extends the framework to track the full photon polarization state and presents the resulting energy- and precession-phase-resolved polarimetric signatures.

title: ERGO-ML and how to directly infer the multi-temperature nature of intra-cluster gas: simulation-based inference with TNG-Cluster
summary: Though galaxy clusters are virialized and mostly in thermodynamic equilibrium, their internal gas thermodynamics are complex. The hot gas is multiphase and spatially inhomogeneous. The exact state of the gas contains important information about the internal physics governing clusters, however, measuring the multiphase distribution of the X-ray emitting gas is hard if not impossible with current observational methods. In this work (part of the ERGO-ML series), we present a direct inference method of the multiphase temperature distribution of the gas in the intra-cluster medium (ICM), applicable over a large range of spatial and mass scales. It works using different spectral resolutions (XRISM-like and Chandra-like) and realistic photon noise. Our method is an application of simulation-based inference. We train a neural-network on X-ray spectra in the range 0.1-10 keV, generated for $\approx 10^5$ sightlines of massive clusters ($M_{\rm 200c} = 10^{14.2-15.2}~\mathrm{M_\odot}$) from the TNG-Cluster cosmological MHD galaxy simulation. We show that our method recovers the mass-weighted temperature of both individual sightlines and entire clusters with an average prediction error of $< 0.01 ~\mathrm{dex}$, and the total gas mass within $0.04 ~\mathrm{dex}$. On top of that it gives accurate measures of the fraction of sub- and super-virial gas. Our method is capable of extracting the cooler gas phase even if the flux contribution is 3 orders of magnitude below that of the virial gas phase. We then show that we can accurately recover the spatial distribution of multi-phase gas both in relaxed and merging systems. This opens the way to studies of the multiphase nature of the ICM and the violent physics of feedback, accretion and merging.

title: Evolving only the observed spacetime region: perfectly parallel lightcone simulations with sCOLA
summary: Cosmological analyses of Stage-IV galaxy surveys require large ensembles of lightcone mock catalogues, but a full survey-scale $N$-body run costs of order $10^7$ CPU hours, putting such ensembles out of reach. We present a framework that produces survey-scale dark matter lightcones for a typical cost of order $10^3$ CPU hours each, based on the spatial COmoving Lagrangian Acceleration (sCOLA) method. sCOLA decomposes an arbitrarily large volume into small tiles that are evolved independently, with buffer regions and non-periodic boundary conditions on the gravitational potential. We combine it with on-the-fly lightcone building, so that the evolved spacetime region reduces to the observed one: each tile is stopped as soon as the observer's past lightcone has left it, and only the tiles intersecting the region of interest are simulated at all. We further introduce two accuracy improvements to the sCOLA formalism: an LPT buffer that approximates the inflow of particles from outside the sCOLA box, and a second-order perturbative approximation to the gravitational potential at its boundaries; together they remove the large-scale inaccuracies of previous work and allow smaller tiles and buffers. Against a \texttt{Gadget4} reference in a $3.84\,h^{-1}\,\mathrm{Gpc}$ box with $3\,840^3$ particles, up to $k \simeq 0.4\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ the sCOLA lightcone reproduces the matter power spectrum to 1%, the velocity divergence power spectrum to 1.5% and the equilateral bispectrum to 2%, with no visible discontinuity at tile boundaries. The run cost $1\,300$ CPU hours, a factor of $2\,600$ below our $\texttt{Gadget4}$ run. Perfect parallelism at this cost brings ensembles of thousands of survey-scale lightcones within reach of a single allocation: $\sim 25\,000$ realisations of the $\textit{Euclid}$ Galactic north cap with a mass resolution of $10^{11}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ for $10^{7}$ CPU hours.

title: Neutrino self-interactions in light of DESI and CMB-SPA
summary: We present an updated analysis of non-standard neutrino self-interactions, where the interaction is effectively mediated by a heavy particle, using the latest available data from DESI and the CMB. The considered data include combinations of DESI DR1 full-shape galaxy clustering (FS), BAO distance measurements, Lyman-$α$ 1D power spectra (Ly-$α$), and a combined CMB likelihood (CMB-SPA) using data from Planck, ACT, and SPT. First, we probe two DESI DR1-only datasets, where the effective interaction parameter $G_{\rm eff}$ is multimodal in the profile likelihood, leading us to analyze two different regimes: moderately interacting (MI$_ν$) and strongly interacting (SI$_ν$) neutrinos. With FS+BAO, the evidence disfavors the SI$_ν$ mode, a trend that becomes slightly stronger with the inclusion of Ly-$α$. However, in the latter dataset, the MI$_ν$ region shows a bimodality in which the intermediate mode is very sharp and peaks around $G_{\rm eff\,} \simeq 10^{-3} \mathrm{MeV}^{-2}$; interestingly, this mode is not penalized versus the weaker standard-like mode. Furthermore, we test CMB and DESI joint data and show that the SI$_ν$ mode is more disfavored by CMB-SPA than by Planck-only data. In particular, the evidence against this mode becomes the strongest thus far (with odds of 5:100000) in the FS+BAO+CMB-SPA combination.

title: Mean-Field Backreaction in Single-Field Inflation
summary: The validity of linear perturbation theory and the role of backreaction in single-field inflationary models that enhance power at small scales have recently been under debate. We investigate scalar backreaction semi-analytically in a mean-field approach within the decoupling limit, considering popular models with a transient ultra-slow-roll (USR) stage or an oscillatory feature (OF) in the potential. We find that ultraviolet (UV) modes in the Bunch--Davies vacuum can substantially affect backreaction estimates unless removed by adiabatic subtraction. Our mean-field treatment can reproduce recent lattice results, but reveals a spurious sensitivity to UV contributions in some cases. This sensitivity is reduced in the OF model when copious particle production separates the amplified physical modes from the UV vacuum tail, making lattice results more reliable in this regime. In USR, instead, adiabatically subtracted spectra yield milder backreaction on the background evolution than previously inferred.

title: Cosmological implications of two mock TianQin standard siren catalogs generated under different background cosmological models
comment: 19 pages, 9 figures, 4 tables. Comments are welcome!
summary: Space-borne gravitational wave (GW) detectors such as TianQin are expected to detect GW standard sirens for cosmological parameter estimation. All previous studies of TianQin adopted the $Λ$CDM model to generate mock standard siren data. In this work, we quantitatively investigate how the choice of background cosmological model affects mock TianQin standard siren (TQSS) catalogs and the corresponding cosmological implications. Adopting the $Λ$CDM model and a redshift-binned dark energy (DE) reconstruction model (the wbin model), we consider the bright standard sirens from massive black hole binary mergers and generate two mock TQSS catalogs, i.e. TQSS1 and TQSS2, respectively. We investigate the difference of the catalogs and further explore their cosmological implications within the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) model, both individually and in combination with DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) data, $\textit{Planck}$ 2018 cosmic microwave background (CMB) data, and DESY5 type Ia supernova (SN Ia) data. We find that there are only small differences between TQSS1 and TQSS2 catalogs, with a maximum relative difference of $1.48\%$ in the distance-redshift relation. In addition, either the TQSS1 or TQSS2 catalog alone gives cosmological constraints similar to those obtained from SN data, implying that these two catalogs can serve as a complement to mainstream cosmological observations. Most importantly, we find that both TQSS1+DESI DR2+CMB+DESY5 and TQSS2+DESI DR2+CMB+DESY5 are still expected to favor dynamical DE, with these two combinations showing a preference for dynamical DE at $2.3σ$ and $3.8σ$, respectively. Adopting different massive black hole seed models does not impact the cosmological implications of the mock TQSS catalogs. Our study indicates the importance of considering different cosmological models in the standard siren forecasts for DE.
